text:
maria: Heads-up — CI is noisy again. Commit hooks are failing ~12 PRs this morning with low-confidence SAST alerts. Link to one: https://redwood.internal/ci/12345/logs :grimacing:

devon: saw that. Most of these look like parser/regex matches on protobuf generator code. False positives.

jamie: Can we stop blocking PRs for low-confidence findings? It's killing dev velocity.

oliver: +1. We should only block on critical/high with exploitability tag. Medium/low -> create ticket and attach to nightly scan.

maria: Agreed. Two asks: (1) a temporary suppression flow for extremely noisy rules, but with audit trail. (2) put the full evidence (stack, file diff, snippet) into the scan artifact instead of dropping it in the PR comment.

devon: For (1) we can add an RBAC role `scan-suppressor` scoped to security leads. That way suppressions are audited. Currently anyone with repo write perms can dismiss findings in GH UI.

jamie: +emoji :thumbsup: Audit logs are crucial. If we add `scan-suppressor` we must record: who suppressed, reason, linked ticket, expiration. Store the record in internal audit log (immutable).

sec-bot: New scan policy change proposed: require `suppression.reason` and `suppression.expiry` fields. Any suppression without those will be auto-reopened after 7 days.

oliver: For (2) we should upload compressed evidence to encrypted storage. KMS + signed URL. The scan pipeline already outputs JSON; just push to artifacts bucket with server-side encryption via KMS.

maria: @oliver can you draft the minimal change to the GitHub Action that uploads artifacts? Want to ensure we keep links in the PR comment but not the full blob in the comment.

oliver: sure. snippet for action below — uploads to `s3://redwood-scans/evidence/` and writes `evidence_url` back into the scan output:```yaml
name: upload-sast-evidence
on: workflow_run
jobs:
  upload:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: |
          tar -czf evidence.tar.gz scans/output.json scans/snippets/
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
        with:
          aws-region: us-west-2
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/scan-uploader
      - run: |
          aws s3 cp evidence.tar.gz s3://redwood-scans/evidence/${{ github.sha }}.tar.gz --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id ${{ secrets.SCAN_KMS_KEY }}
      - run: echo "evidence_url=https://evidence.redwood.internal/${{ github.sha }}.tar.gz" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
```

jamie: That looks good. Make sure the uploader role is restricted to `PutObject` and `PutObjectTagging` only. No list/delete.

devon: Also add a small checksum field in the scan JSON so any later tampering is detectable. HMAC with KMS-managed key.

maria: What about the commit-hook flakiness? Until the policy lands, can we move non-blocking rules to `warn` level in pre-merge checks and keep `fail` only on high/critical?

sre-oncall: From infra side, note that shifting to nightly may increase storage by ~5GB/day. Cost is fine but let's add expiry (30d) and lifecycle rules.

sec-bot: CI scan report uploaded: scan-id=scan-2026-04-12-003, findings=14, high=1, medium=3, low=10. Artifact: https://evidence.redwood.internal/scan-2026-04-12-003.tar.gz

maria: Thanks @sec-bot. I'll open a formal RFC for the suppression RBAC + evidence pipeline change and link to this thread.

jamie: For incident readiness: if a suppressed finding is later re-opened as exploitable (via fuzz or DAST), we should auto-create an incident and notify `#oncall-incidents`. Add that to the RFC.

oliver: I'll add the HMAC and retention lifecycle to the RFC appendix and a sample IAM policy.

maria: Plan: (A) change pre-merge rule levels today to reduce noise; (B) draft RFC for `scan-suppressor` RBAC + KMS-encrypted evidence + audit trail by EOD; (C) implement artifact uploader + HMAC next sprint.

devon: ping me if you need review on RBAC YAML.

maria: thanks everyone. Filing ticket: SEC-8342 and linking to this thread. :white_check_mark:
